accepted.s: The Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) was launched in which year as an initiative of the Indian Navy?
accepted.x: IONS was launched in 2008 as an initiative of the Indian Navy.
accepted.tq: Direct year-based recall of an institutional fact.
accepted.sec: IONS; Indian Ocean militarisation and foreign bases

accepted.s: The first meeting of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) was held at:
accepted.x: The first IONS meeting was held in New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Direct place-based recall.
accepted.sec: IONS; Indian Ocean militarisation and foreign bases

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature and activities of IONS?
o: It is a United Nations body concerned exclusively with piracy trials.
It is a compulsory military alliance concerned exclusively with naval warfare.
It is a voluntary forum covering maritime security, maritime domain awareness and HADR.
It is a treaty-based organisation dealing only with energy security.
accepted.x: IONS is a voluntary forum covering maritime security, maritime domain awareness and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the forum’s mandate from treaty-based or military-alliance institutions.
accepted.sec: IONS; Indian Ocean militarisation and foreign bases

accepted.s: The 9th Conclave of Chiefs of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium was hosted at:
accepted.x: India hosted the 9th IONS Conclave of Chiefs at Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Current institutional event and venue recall.
accepted.sec: IONS; Indian Ocean militarisation and foreign bases

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Diego Garcia — US-UK facility in the Chagos Archipelago
Camp Lemonnier — Chinese naval base in Sri Lanka
Djibouti base — Russian first overseas base
String of Pearls — Indian network of Arctic ports
accepted.x: Diego Garcia is a US-UK facility located in the Chagos Archipelago. The other pairs wrongly identify the country or the strategic concept.
accepted.tq: Use the location-country-function relationship to eliminate swapped-base options.
accepted.sec: IONS; Indian Ocean militarisation and foreign bases

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets is associated with the concept of China’s ‘String of Pearls’?
accepted.x: Gwadar, Hambantota and Djibouti are associated with the String of Pearls concept.
accepted.tq: Group-recognition question using a known strategic cluster.
accepted.sec: IONS; Indian Ocean militarisation and foreign bases

accepted.s: Djibouti hosts which combination of facilities?
o: Russia’s first overseas base and the UK’s Diego Garcia facility
India’s first overseas base and France’s naval headquarters
China’s first overseas base and the US Camp Lemonnier
Japan’s first overseas base and Australia’s Camp Talisman
accepted.x: Djibouti hosts China’s first overseas base, established in 2017, and the US Camp Lemonnier.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely associated foreign military facilities by country.
accepted.sec: IONS; Indian Ocean militarisation and foreign bases

accepted.s: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched on 30 November 2015 at:
o: The G20 Summit in New Delhi
accepted.x: The ISA was launched on 30 November 2015 at COP21 in Paris.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Solar Alliance:
1. It is treaty-based.
2. Its headquarters is at Gurugram.
3. It aims to mobilise one trillion US dollars of solar investment by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: ISA is treaty-based, headquartered at Gurugram, and has a one-trillion-dollar solar investment mobilisation goal for 2030.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of institutional status, headquarters and quantitative target.
accepted.sec: Energy groupings - ISA, OSOWOG, GBA, IEA

accepted.s: The stated membership of the International Solar Alliance in 2024 was:

accepted.s: Under UNCLOS 1982, the territorial sea extends up to:

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Continental shelf — exactly 200 nautical miles in every case
accepted.x: The EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles. The contiguous zone extends to 24 nautical miles, the territorial sea to 12 nautical miles, and the continental shelf may extend up to 350 nautical miles.

accepted.s: The contiguous zone under UNCLOS extends up to how many nautical miles from the baseline?

accepted.s: The continental shelf may extend up to:

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the comparison between India’s strategic petroleum reserve buffer and the IEA benchmark mentioned in current maritime-energy discussions?
o: India has a 90-day buffer against the IEA’s 9.5-day benchmark.
India has a 9.5-day buffer against the IEA’s 90-day benchmark.
India has no strategic petroleum reserve while the IEA prescribes 9.5 days.
Both India and the IEA prescribe a 30-day buffer.
accepted.x: The stated comparison is a thin Indian SPR buffer of 9.5 days against the IEA’s 90-day benchmark.
accepted.tq: Compare two figures directly and avoid reversing the benchmark and the domestic position.
